:::{#exm-gd-quadratic-error}
#### The error multiplier for a step length of one quarter

```{r}
#| label: gd-quadratic-error-r
#| echo: false
gdq_s_pe <- 0.25
gdq_eigs_pe <- c(3, 1)
gdq_factors_pe <- 1 - gdq_s_pe * gdq_eigs_pe
gdq_abs_pe <- abs(gdq_factors_pe)
gdq_rho_pe <- max(gdq_abs_pe)
```

Let $\matr{S} = \sbmat{ 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 }$ with [eigenvalues](linear-algebra.qmd#def-eigenvalue) $3$ and $1$
([eigenvalue example](linear-algebra.qmd#exm-eigenvalue)),
and $\vecf{c} = \vzero_{2 \times 1}$,
so $\vx^* = \vzero_{2 \times 1}$.
With $\steplen = `{r} gdq_s_pe`$, the factors $1 - \steplen\,\eigval_i$ are
$`{r} gdq_factors_pe[1]`$ and $`{r} gdq_factors_pe[2]`$,
so $\convrate(\steplen) = `{r} gdq_rho_pe`$ and

$$
\norm{\iterpoint{\vx}{t}} \le `{r} gdq_rho_pe`^t\,\norm{\iterpoint{\vx}{0}}.
$$

Along the [eigenvector](linear-algebra.qmd#def-eigenvector) for $\eigval = 3$ the [error](#def-iterate-error) shrinks fast,
and along the eigenvector for $\eigval = 1$ it shrinks slowly;
the [bound](sets.qmd#def-bound) follows the slower one.

:::
